title: Human LV endocardial optical mapping · donor 1
citation: Smirnov D, Pikunov A, Syunyaev R, et al. Genetic algorithm-based personalized models of human cardiac action potential. PLoS ONE 15(5):e0231695 (2020).
preparation: Discarded donor human posterolateral left-ventricular wedge; endocardial surface, epicardial bipolar pacing.
conditions: 37 °C oxygenated Tyrode; di-4-ANBDQBS voltage-sensitive dye; 10–15 µM blebbistatin; 100 s steady-state pacing; cycle length 1000 ms.
signal: Polarity already inverted in source cmosData; increasing stored signal is depolarization. Displayed as locally normalized optical signal, 0=baseline,1=peak; not mV.
time_unit: ms from the start of a 1000 ms window; pacing trigger approximately 100 ms; individual pixel activation timing preserved.
single_beat_layout: Same encoding as voltage; single beat at documented start index; default voltage is the four-beat ensemble.
timing_layout: little-endian float32 [map,y,x]; maps AT,RT80,APD80,RT90,APD90,SNR; excluded pixels NaN
processing: Use four 1000 ms beats, aligned to the measured global pacing trigger; no site-specific time alignment.
Apply a narrow 60 Hz IIR notch (Q=30), zero-phase forward-backward, to the full 4096 ms recording.
Ensemble-average four beats. Apply an 11 ms cubic Savitzky–Golay temporal filter. No spatial smoothing.
Subtract linear baseline drift using resting medians at 10–49 ms and 800–949 ms.
Normalize each pixel between its local baseline and maximum at 100–449 ms.
AT is the maximum first derivative at 100–299 ms, estimated by an additional 11 ms cubic Savitzky–Golay derivative.
RT80 and RT90 are the first descending 20% and 10% crossings after the local post-activation peak, linearly interpolated.
Quality mask: background >10% of its 99th percentile, amplitude ≥6 source counts, amplitude/residual noise ≥5, APD80 between 140 and 650 ms, valid AT; retain largest connected component.
Export every second frame (2 ms), with 8-bit quantization between −0.25 and 1.25 normalized units. Timing maps use native 1 ms samples.
Optional individual beat uses the same filtering and baseline correction, without ensemble averaging.
limitations: Optical pixels average fluorescence from tissue volumes; these are not individual cells.
Optical amplitude is not calibrated to transmembrane millivolts.
This is an isolated human wedge endocardial surface, not a whole-heart recovery map.
No ECG channel identity or calibration is documented; auxiliary analog channels are not presented as ECG.
Derived timing depends on filtering, thresholds and quality masks. A 1 ms sampling interval does not imply 1 ms physiological accuracy.
No anatomical orientation labels are invented for the camera image.
Only one pacing condition and a short recording are represented; neither donor represents a normal population.
Optical scattering can distort the upstroke and broaden spatial sampling.
